dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Nam, can you lend me five hundred baht? I'm broke until Friday.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, kən juː ˈlɛnd miː ˈfaɪv ˈhʌndrəd ˈbɑːt? aɪm ˈbroʊk ənˈtɪl ˈfraɪdeɪ.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Thanks! I'll pay you back on Friday, I promise.
dialogue.reading: ˈθæŋks! aɪl ˈpeɪ juː ˈbæk ɑːn ˈfraɪdeɪ, aɪ ˈprɑːmɪs.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: No problem. Oh, and can I borrow your laptop this evening? Mine isn't working.
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ ˈprɑːbləm. ˈoʊ, ənd kən aɪ ˈbɑːroʊ jʊr ˈlæptɑːp ˈðɪs ˈiːvnɪŋ? ˈmaɪn ˈɪzənt ˈwɜːrkɪŋ.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Of course. You lent me money, so I'll lend you my laptop!
dialogue.reading: əv ˈkɔːrs. juː ˈlɛnt miː ˈmʌni, soʊ aɪl ˈlɛnd juː maɪ ˈlæptɑːp!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Emma, can I ask you something? Do you often borrow money?
dialogue.reading: ˈɛmə, kən aɪ ˈæsk juː ˈsʌmθɪŋ? duː juː ˈɔːfən ˈbɑːroʊ ˈmʌni?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Not often. But I have a student loan in Canada, so I have some debt.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːt ˈɔːfən. bʌt aɪ ˈhæv ə ˈstuːdənt ˈloʊn ɪn ˈkænədə, soʊ aɪ ˈhæv sʌm ˈdɛt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: A loan? How much do you owe?
dialogue.reading: ə ˈloʊn? ˈhaʊ ˈmʌtʃ duː juː ˈoʊ?

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: About ten thousand dollars. I'll pay it back after I graduate.
dialogue.reading: əˈbaʊt ˈtɛn ˈθaʊzənd ˈdɑːlərz. aɪl ˈpeɪ ɪt ˈbæk ˈæftər aɪ ˈɡrædʒueɪt.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: That's a lot of debt! In Thailand, many students borrow money from the government, too.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ə ˈlɑːt əv ˈdɛt! ɪn ˈtaɪlænd, ˈmɛni ˈstuːdənts ˈbɑːroʊ ˈmʌni frəm ðə ˈɡʌvərnmənt, ˈtuː.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Yes. So don't worry. You're not the only one!
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs. soʊ ˈdoʊnt ˈwɜːri. jʊr ˈnɑːt ði ˈoʊnli ˈwʌn!
